note: Curated Yamuna timeline for the Delhi rivers surface - court orders, instruments, floods and programme milestones, each with a dated citation (URLs verified live 2026-07-20 unless noted bot-blocked). The contested Sept-2025 Hathnikund peak figure is referenced without a number pending resolution.

events.title: Five states sign the upper-Yamuna MoU - Delhi's share fixed 'interim', still operative
events.summary: The 12 May 1994 MoU apportioned the upper Yamuna's flows and created the Upper Yamuna River Board as steward. Delhi's share: 0.724 BCM/yr, with drinking water served first in deficit years. Three decades later the 'interim seasonal allocation' remains the constitution of Delhi's water supply.

events.title: NGT's 'Maily Se Nirmal Yamuna' judgment in Manoj Misra v Union of India
events.summary: The landmark rejuvenation order in OA 6/2012 - India's longest-running river docket - directing phased sewage interception, floodplain protection and a rejuvenation plan. The Yamuna Monitoring Committee (Shailaja Chandra + B.S. Sajwan) followed in 2018; its reports remain the docket's institutional memory.

events.title: The river takes the Ring Road: 208.66 m, highest ever recorded
events.summary: On 13 July 2023 the Yamuna crossed 208.66 m at the Old Railway Bridge - 1.17 m above the 45-year-old 1978 record - flooding Civil Lines, ITO and Rajghat and forcing ~27,000 evacuations. The CWC's own case study is the official post-mortem; the ITO barrage's jammed gates became the proximate-cause story.

events.title: Manoj Misra (1956-2023) dies the day a Yamuna Sansad convenes
events.summary: The forester-turned-advocate who founded Yamuna Jiye Abhiyaan (2007) and carried OA 6/2012 through eleven years died on 4 June 2023 in Bhopal - the same day a citizens' Yamuna Parliament met in Delhi to demand the river's revival.

events.title: Delhi HC declines Chhath at the Yamuna: too polluted to pray in
events.summary: Citing pollution, the High Court refused permission for Chhath rituals on the river bank - a judicial certification of the river's condition delivered against the festival that most publicly depends on it. The Kalindi Kunj froth imagery returns every October-November.

events.title: DJB concedes to NGT: 75% of STPs cannot disinfect
events.summary: In OA 183/2024 (taken up from press reporting), DJB's sworn status report conceded that three-quarters of its sewage plants lack disinfection equipment - meaning even 'treated' effluent can carry faecal bacteria to the river. The CAG separately found 25 STPs' effluent failing DPCC norms.

events.title: CAG's DJB audit tabled: NRW 51-53%, Rs 66,595 cr debt, augmentation 'remote'
events.summary: Report No. 3 of 2025 (tabled 23 March 2026) put audit-grade numbers on the system feeding the river: 212.59 MGD of colony sewage entering storm drains untreated, effluent from 25 STPs failing norms, no flow meters anywhere in the chain, and Rs 4,988 crore lost to non-revenue water.

events.title: Mission Sahibi launches: dredging 9.1 million cubic metres from the Najafgarh drain
events.summary: After a bathymetric survey of the 57-km drain, the government deployed 32 machines including Finnish amphibious dredgers to restore carrying capacity - both a pollution intervention and pre-monsoon insurance. The name itself concedes the drain is the buried Sahibi river.

events.title: The 39-drain trapping deadline passes without a public word
events.summary: March 2026 reporting had 17 drains trapped and 22 in progress against a 30 June 2026 completion target. The deadline passed with no known public completion announcement; DPCC's own May 2026 monthly showed 9 of 39 monitored drain points at NO FLOW - the trapping programme's verifiable footprint, and the number to watch in each new monthly report.

events.title: A 2023-like flood spell repeats within two years
events.summary: September 2025 brought another evacuation-scale Yamuna spell driven by very high Hathnikund discharge (the exact peak figure is reported inconsistently across sources and is deliberately not stated here). SANDRP's analysis of why 2023's lessons had not changed outcomes is the sharpest public account.
